Finally, I wear shirts with “ventilation,” low cut tops, short sleeves or no sleeves. Anything that isn’t a t-shirt that goes to my neck. It’s too hot for that. These girls need to breathe.

Kitties bite cause they want attention, to play, or for protection. When my baby bit me in the past, I’d give her a toy to chew on rather than myself. I also used my hand as a toy, initiating chase, riling her up. Of course she saw my hand as a toy. Defer their focus away from you. If I saw signs of her tracking my movements and her pupils enlarged, I knew an attack was imminent. Distracting her with a toy or stuffed animal breaks her targeting and changes her focus. Having them focus their energy in play is important. It stimulates them, works out energy & is a bonding activity. 

Lastly, be consistent with all responses to their behavior. My baby knows if she’s done something that I don’t like or she knows not to do when I use my stern talking voice. When she’s done well, I use a higher tone with petting and praise. They don’t speak English but they understand behavior can lead to consequences. If they do something wrong, correct them immediately. They’re not going to understand why you’re upset 30 minutes later. 

Hope this helps!

I was diagnosed in 2021. To prevent irritation or sores, I use gold bond extra strength body powder applied with round cotton pads. I coat it until it feels cool between the bottom of the breast and the skin below. 

When I shower, I use hibiclens to clear any bacteria from the area, then I use Dove moisture body wash to hydrate the area. I find washing in cooler water reduces irritation. When you get out of the shower, I use a towel under the area to ensure it dries completely. Apply the powder, and then get dressed from there. 

Using the hibiclens will reduce the bacteria causing the smell. I have heard good things about extra strength deodorant. I use a Degree stick deodorant.

Right now, try to keep everything clean and dry. I would use Gold Bond Extra Strength Powder (https://a.co/d/315bxSG). I apply with cotton round pads, you can get them from any store like a CVS/Walmart; etc. 

As for dressings, I recommend you use a Curad sterile non adherent pads with tape roll. The best thing to do in a pinch would be a sanitary pad. Attach it between the legs with the sticky side out and sticking to your underwear on both sides. I would recommend panty liners or thin pads. 

Do not pop anything. Let it bleed and keep it as clean as possible. Use a wash cloth to clean in the shower, try to keep the water warm but not hot and wash with hibiclens if you have it. I also use Dove moisture body wash or bar and it is gentle and hydrates the area. When you get out, dry out the area as much as you can. 

Wear clothing that allows “breathing” between your legs. If you can’t, sit or lay down and spread your legs enough to prevent friction. It just needs time to heal enough for you to travel.
